name: 10-Ball Pool
description: Pool (pocket billiards) discipline where balls 1 to 10 must be pocketed in order; the called 10-ball last wins the rack.

name: 10m Air Pistol Shooting
description: Olympic precision shooting event: one-handed shots from a compressed-air pistol at a target 10 meters away.

name: 10m Air Rifle Shooting
description: Olympic precision shooting event: standing shots from a compressed-air rifle at a target 10 meters away.

name: 24 Hours of Le Mans
description: World-famous 24-hour endurance car race on the Circuit de la Sarthe in France; the car covering the most distance wins.

name: 25m Rapid Fire Pistol Shooting
description: ISSF shooting event with timed 4-second strings at a turning target 25 meters away; Olympic event since 1896.

name: 360ball
description: Young South African racquet sport on a circular court where players bounce the ball off a central disc.

name: 3D Archery
description: Archery on outdoor courses at unmarked distances, shooting at life-size animal replicas in foam; governed by World Archery.

name: 3x3 Basketball
description: Basketball on a half court with one basket, three players per team and a 12-second shot clock; Olympic since 2020.

name: 3x3 Wheelchair Basketball
description: 3x3 basketball adapted for wheelchair athletes and governed by the IWBF; Paralympic event since Tokyo 2020.

name: 50m Rifle 3 Positions Shooting
description: ISSF rifle event with shots from prone, standing and kneeling at 50 meters; Olympic staple since 1960.

name: 8-Ball Pool
description: The classic pool game: players clear their group of seven balls and then pocket the black 8-ball to win.

name: 9-Ball Pool
description: Professional pool game where balls 1 to 9 are played in order and pocketing the yellow 9-ball wins the rack.

name: AFL 9s
description: Nine-a-side variant of Australian rules football played on a smaller field, popular in schools and at festivals.

name: AFLX
description: Shortened, faster variant of Australian rules football with six players per side on a smaller oval.

name: Acrobatic Gymnastics
description: Gymnastics discipline where pairs or groups perform acrobatic lifts, throws and balances, judged on difficulty and execution.

name: Adventure Racing
description: Multisport endurance races combining running, mountain biking, paddling and navigation through wilderness over several days.

name: Aerobic Gymnastics
description: Gymnastics discipline with high-intensity aerobic routines of strength, flexibility and jumps performed to music.

name: Aeromodelling
description: Sport of designing, building and flying remote-controlled model aircraft, with competitions for flight performance and scale.

name: Aggressive Inline Skating
description: Roller sport performing grinds, airs and rail tricks on inline skates at skateparks and street spots; contested at X Games and world championships.

name: Agility Dog Sport
description: Dog sport where handlers guide their dogs through a timed obstacle course of jumps, tunnels and contact obstacles.

name: Air Guitar
description: Performance competition where contestants mime playing an invisible guitar to music, judged on technique and stage presence.

name: Air Hockey
description: Table game where players use mallets to shoot a puck into the opponent's goal on a low-friction air-cushioned table.

name: Air Racing
description: Aeroplane racing: aircraft race around pylons or circuits at low altitude; FAI classes and pylon racing series since the 1920s.

name: AirBadminton
description: Outdoor badminton variant played with a lighter shuttlecock (AirShuttle) that works on grass, sand or hard courts.

name: Alpine Skiing Downhill
description: Fastest alpine skiing discipline: one timed run down a steep course at speeds over 130 km/h.

name: Alpine Skiing Giant Slalom
description: Alpine skiing race with wide turns around gates on a long course; two runs on different courses.

name: Alpine Skiing Slalom
description: Alpine skiing's most technical race: the shortest course with the tightest turns around a series of gates.

name: Alpine Skiing Super-G
description: Alpine skiing speed event between downhill and giant slalom, with fewer but wider turns on a long course.

name: American Football
description: Contact team sport where teams score by carrying or passing an oval ball into the opponent's end zone; the NFL is the top league.

name: Amputee Football
description: Football (soccer) adapted for players with limb amputations, played on crutches with modified offside rules.

name: Aquabike
description: Personal watercraft racing on jet skis, with runabout and ski sprint classes plus freestyle; UIM Aquabike world championship.

name: Aquathlon
description: Race combining open-water swimming and running, usually a 2.5 km swim followed by a 10 km run.

name: Archery
description: Precision sport of shooting arrows at a target; Olympic disciplines are recurve and compound at 70 meters.

name: Arctic Sports
description: Traditional Inuit events of the Arctic Winter Games: one and two foot high kick, Alaskan high kick, kneel jump, knuckle hop, arm pull and more.

name: Arctic Winter Games
description: Biennial circumpolar multisport and cultural festival for northern youth held since 1970; blends winter sports with Arctic Sports and Dene Games.

name: Areca Nut Tree Climbing
description: Traditional South and Southeast Asian competition to climb tall areca palm trees as fast as possible.

name: Arena Football
description: Indoor variant of American football played on a small padded field, originally staged in arenas.

name: Arm Wrestling
description: Strength duel at a table: two athletes lock hands and try to pin the opponent arm; professional world circuit under the World Armwrestling League.

name: Artistic Cycling
description: Gymnastics on a fixed-gear bicycle performing figures, jumps and balances; official UCI indoor cycling discipline with world championships.

name: Artistic Swimming
description: Aquatic discipline combining swimming, dance and gymnastics in choreographed routines, formerly called synchronized swimming.

name: Athletics
description: Track and field: running, jumping and throwing events, from the 100 m sprint to the marathon and the decathlon.

name: Australian Rules Football
description: Contact ball sport on a large oval with 18 players per side; hugely popular in Australia and governed by the AFL.

name: Autocross
description: Timed motorsport event where drivers navigate a cone course one at a time on pavement, also called Solo.

name: Axe Throwing
description: Target sport of throwing hatchets at wooden targets for points; standardized in world leagues (WATL, IATL).

name: BASE Jumping
description: Extreme sport of parachuting from fixed objects such as cliffs, buildings, bridges and antennas.

name: BMX Freestyle
description: BMX cycling with acrobatic tricks on ramps, rails and in skateparks; Olympic discipline since 2008.

name: BMX Racing
description: BMX bikes racing on a dirt track with jumps and banked turns; Olympic sport since 2008.

name: Backgammon
description: Ancient two-player board game of strategy and luck where checkers are moved around 24 points and borne off.

name: Backhold Wrestling
description: Traditional Scottish wrestling hold where both wrestlers grip each other's backs; first to touch the ground loses.

name: Badminton
description: Fast racquet sport with a shuttlecock over a net; smashes can exceed 400 km/h; Olympic since 1992.

name: Baja 1000
description: Legendary off-road endurance race across Mexico's Baja California peninsula for cars, trucks, ATVs and motorcycles.

name: Ball Hockey
description: Indoor team sport like ice hockey but played in gym shoes with a ball instead of skates and a puck.

name: Balle Pelote
description: Basque pelota variant played with the bare hand, a leather glove or a basket against a wall.

name: Banana Ball
description: Hybrid of handball and dodgeball played with a soft ball, popular at summer camps.

name: Bandy
description: Ice team sport with 11 players a side, a small ball and football-style rules on a large rink; world championships since 1957 (FIB).

name: Bare-knuckle Boxing
description: Prizefighting boxing without gloves under historical London Prize Ring lineages, revived by sanctioned promotions such as BKFC.

name: Barebow Archery
description: Archery shot without a sight, usually with a simple recurve or longbow, aiming instinctively.

name: Barefoot Water Skiing
description: Water skiing on the bare feet at higher speeds (about 35-45 km/h); IWWF tournament discipline with world championships.

name: Barrel Racing
description: Rodeo timed event where horse and rider race a cloverleaf pattern around three barrels.

name: Baseball
description: Bat-and-ball team sport where the batting side scores runs by running around four bases; MLB is the top US league.

name: Baseball5
description: Street version of baseball played with a rubber ball on a small diamond with five players per team.

name: Basketball
description: Team sport where players score by throwing a ball through the opponent's hoop; the NBA is the top league and it has been Olympic since 1936.

name: Basque Pelota
description: Basque wall-ball family played with the hand, a leather glove, basket or wooden bat against a fronton wall; Olympic demonstration 1992.

name: Bat and Trap
description: Historic English shooting sport where clay pigeons are launched by a spring arm and shot with a muzzle-loading gun.

name: Beach Handball
description: Handball played on sand with smaller teams and goals; faster and more spectacular than the indoor game.

name: Beach Korfball
description: Korfball variant played on sand, usually 4v4 on a smaller court, at beach tournaments.

name: Beach Rugby
description: Rugby on sand between teams of five or seven, with quick taps, high scoring and festival formats such as the Uruguay-hosted world series stops.

name: Beach Soccer
description: Soccer on sand with five players per side, small goals and spectacular overhead kicks.

name: Beach Sprint Rowing
description: Rowing race of 500 m to 1 km on flat water in single sculls, starting and finishing on the beach.

name: Beach Tennis
description: Tennis played on a sand court with solid paddles and a low net, usually in doubles.

name: Beach Volleyball
description: Two-a-side volleyball on sand over a slightly higher net; Olympic since Atlanta 1996 and FIVB world tour headline sport.

name: Beach Volleyball 4x4
description: Beach volleyball with four players per team, used in some youth and amateur tournaments.

name: Beach Wrestling
description: Wrestling matches in a circular sand arena, similar to Olympic-style wrestling but on the beach.

name: Bed Racing
description: Novelty team race where crews push decorated wheeled beds around a course; a charity fixture of British town calendars.

name: Belt Wrestling
description: Traditional wrestling variant where competitors grip each other's belts instead of clothing or limbs.

name: Belt Wrestling Alysh
description: Kyrgyz belt wrestling ( Alysh ) where wrestlers hold each other's belts and the first to fall loses.

name: Biathle
description: Three-stage competition of swimming, running and shooting, derived from military training.

name: Biathlon
description: Olympic winter sport combining cross-country skiing with .22 rifle shooting; IBU world cup and world championships.

name: Bike Polo
description: Team sport like field polo but played on bicycles with mallets on a hard-court pitch.

name: Bike Trial
description: Bicycle or motorcycle sport where riders navigate obstacle courses without touching their feet down.

name: Bikejoring
description: Dog sport in which one or two harnessed dogs tow a cyclist along dirt trails; IFSS dryland racing discipline.

name: Billiards
description: Cue sports played on a cloth-covered table, including snooker, carom and the pool disciplines.

name: Blackball
description: Pool variant popular in the UK and China where the black 8-ball must be pocketed last to win.

name: Blind Football
description: Paralympic 5-a-side football for visually impaired players, played with a ball containing bells; governed by IBSA.

name: Blind Tennis
description: Tennis for visually impaired players, using a louder ball and allowing fewer bounces.

name: Bo-taoshi
description: Japanese capture-the-flag game in which teams of up to 75 attack and defend a pole; played at military and university festivals.

name: Bobsleigh
description: Winter team sliding sport on an icy track; competed in two-person and four-person variants; also called bobsled.

name: Bocce
description: Italian boules-style game where players roll or throw balls to land closest to a small target ball (pallino).

name: Bocce Punto
description: Fast bocce variant where the pallino and balls may be moved or knocked away after every throw.

name: Bocce Raffa
description: Bocce variant where players may knock away opponents' balls with their own ball, adding a tactical element.

name: Bocce Volo
description: Bocce variant with a run-up, trying to stop the ball as close as possible to the pallino.

name: Boccia
description: Paralympic precision ball sport similar to boules for athletes with severe disabilities, played with leather balls on a court.

name: Bodyboarding
description: Board sport where riders lie prone on a short foam board and ride breaking waves toward the shore.

name: Bodybuilding
description: Competitive sport judged on muscular size, symmetry and definition through poses; Mr. Olympia is the top event.

name: Bodysurfing
description: Surfing without a board: riders use their body, hand planes and swim fins to ride waves.

name: Bog Snorkelling
description: Competitive snorkelling through a muddy peat-bog course in Wales, using flippers but no diving gear.

name: Bokator
description: Ancient Khmer martial art from Cambodia with powerful strikes, joint locks and animal-style forms.

name: Bossaball
description: Team ball sport on inflatables combining volleyball, football and gymnastics, played with trampolines and set to music.

name: Bottle-kicking
description: Traditional Flemish team game where a bottle on a wooden block is knocked over with a thrown ball.

name: Bouldering
description: Ropeless climbing on short walls with crash pads, judged on fewest attempts; Olympic combined climbing discipline since Tokyo 2020.

name: Boule Lyonnaise
description: Variant of pétanque with a run-up where the ball is in motion, played mainly in southeastern France.

name: Bowling
description: Game of rolling a ball down a lane to knock down ten pins; ten-pin bowling has professional PBA tours.

name: Box Lacrosse
description: Indoor lacrosse played in a hockey rink with boards, six players per side and a rubber ball.

name: Boxing
description: Combat sport of punches with padded gloves in weight classes and rounds; Olympic since 1904.

name: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu
description: Ground-fighting martial art emphasizing leverage and submissions (chokes, joint locks) against larger opponents.

name: Breaking
description: Acrobatic hip hop dance style from the Bronx, contested in b-boy and b-girl battles; Olympic debut at Paris 2024 under the WDSF.

name: British Baseball
description: Bat-and-ball game similar to rounders, played mainly in Wales and England with four bases.

name: Broom Hockey
description: Informal ice hockey variant played with brooms and a ball instead of sticks and a puck.

name: Broomball
description: Team sport on ice or a gym floor played with a ball and broom-like sticks, no skates required.

name: Brännboll
description: Scandinavian bat-and-ball game similar to baseball, played with a soft ball and a flat bat.

name: Bubble Gum Blowing
description: Competition to blow the biggest bubble with chewing gum, judged by diameter; world championships exist.

name: Buhurt
description: Armoured medieval combat in formation or duels with blunted steel weapons; HMBIA world championships (Battle of the Nations).

name: Bullet Racing
description: Vintage motorcycle sprint races on straight beach or track courses, popular in the early 20th century.

name: Bökh
description: Traditional Mongolian wrestling with up to 1024 competitors in a single-elimination tournament and no weight classes.

name: Caber Toss
description: Scottish Highland Games event: throwing a tall tapered log end over end so it lands aligned with the thrower.

name: Cable Wakeboarding
description: Wakeboarding towed by an overhead cable system instead of a boat, at cable parks.

name: Calcio Fiorentino
description: Historical Florentine football combining football, rugby and wrestling, revived as a tournament in Florence each June.

name: Calisthenics
description: Training and competition based on bodyweight exercises such as pull-ups, dips and muscle-ups; street workout is the competitive form.

name: Camel Jumping
description: Traditional sport of the Arabian Peninsula where athletes leap over the backs of standing camels.

name: Camel Racing
description: Desert racing sport, today with robot jockeys, governed by national federations; major meetings in the Gulf states.

name: Cammag
description: Traditional stick-and-ball game of the Isle of Man, similar to hurling or shinty.

name: Camogie
description: Women's variant of hurling played in Ireland under the Camogie Association; intercounty championships at Croke Park.

name: Canadian Football
description: Football variant with 12 players per side, three downs and a larger field; the CFL is the top league.

name: Canal Vaulting
description: Dutch sport of pole vaulting over canals, a traditional spring festival activity in Friesland.

name: Canarian Wrestling
description: Lucha canaria, the traditional wrestling of the Canary Islands, won by unbalancing the opponent to touch the sand with any body part.

name: Canicross
description: Cross-country running with a dog harnessed to the runner by a bungee line, popular across Europe.

name: Canine Freestyle
description: Dog sport: choreographed routines of tricks, heelwork and jumps performed to music with the dog.

name: Canoe Freestyle
description: Canoeing discipline where paddlers perform acrobatic tricks and spins in standing waves or on flat water.

name: Canoe Marathon
description: Long-distance canoe or kayak racing over 20 to 30 km, with portages around obstacles.

name: Canoe Ocean Racing
description: Surfski, sea kayak and outrigger racing on open ocean courses with downwind wave riding; ICF ocean racing worlds.

name: Canoe Polo
description: Ball sport in kayaks on pool or flat water: teams of five pass and shoot into goals suspended above the water; ICF world championships.

name: Canoe Slalom
description: Whitewater canoeing or kayaking down a rapids course through hanging gates, scored on time and penalties.

name: Canoe Sprint
description: Flat-water racing of kayaks and canoes over 200 m to 5000 m; Olympic core discipline since 1936 (ICF).

name: Canoeing
description: Paddling sport with open canoes (single-blade paddle) and kayaks (double blade) on flat water, whitewater or the sea.

name: Canopy Piloting
description: Skydiving discipline where jumpers steer their open parachute canopies through a course of gates.

name: Canyoning
description: Adventure sport of descending canyons by hiking, climbing, rappelling, swimming and sliding down waterfalls.

name: Capoeira
description: Afro-Brazilian art combining martial arts, acrobatics and music in a roda (circle); UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.

name: Carjitsu
description: Hybrid martial art combining judo, jiu-jitsu, karate and wrestling techniques, founded in the UK.

name: Carom Billiards
description: Cue sport on a pocketless table: the cue ball must hit both object balls, and a cushion before the second ball in most variants.

name: Carrom
description: Indian tabletop game of flicking a striker to sink coins into corner pockets; international federations hold world championships.

name: Castells
description: Catalan tradition of building human towers several stories high, topped by a child called the enxaneta.

name: Catch Wrestling
description: Professional wrestling style with unlimited submissions and pinfalls, the basis of modern pro wrestling.

name: Cerebral Palsy Football
description: Football (7-a-side) for players with cerebral palsy under adapted rules; Paralympic sport.

name: Chariot Racing
description: Ancient Olympic sport where charioteers raced two- or four-horse chariots around a hippodrome.

name: Cheese Rolling
description: Gravity race down the steep Cooper Hill in Gloucestershire chasing a cheese wheel; contested since the early 1800s.

name: Cherry Pit Spitting
description: Distance-spitting contest of cherry pits, most famously at the International Cherry Pit Spitting Championship in Eau Claire, Michigan.

name: Chess
description: Two-player strategy board game on 64 squares with 16 pieces per side; world championship since 1886.

name: Chess Boxing
description: Hybrid bout alternating rounds of chess and boxing; a fighter wins by checkmate, KO or referee decision (WCBO).

name: Chinese Eight-Ball
description: Pool variant popular in China and the UK, played on a snooker-sized table with eight-ball rules.

name: Chinlone
description: Traditional Burmese sport where a woven rattan ball is kept in the air by a circle of players using feet, knees and hands.

name: Chovgan
description: Ancient Persian polo-like game on horseback, ancestor of modern polo, still played in Azerbaijan.

name: Coastal Rowing
description: Rowing in sea-going boats along the coast, in fixed-seat or sliding-seat shells.

name: Coasteering
description: Adventure sport combining cliff climbing, scrambling, swimming and jumping along a rocky coastline.

name: Coffin Wars
description: Novelty grappling format of the Pro League Network: two fighters take turns trying to escape from a reinforced coffin; league debuted in 2024.

name: Combat Ju-Jitsu
description: Self-defense system combining striking, throwing and ground fighting, used in military and police training.

name: Combat Sambo
description: Martial art and sport derived from sambo, with throws, locks and strikes; international championships exist.

name: Combined Driving
description: Equestrian three-phase event (dressage, marathon, cones) with horse-drawn carriages.

name: Competitive Eating
description: Contests to eat the most food in a set time; the Nathan's Hot Dog Contest is the most famous.

name: Competitive Sleeping
description: Satirical 'sport' of sleeping the longest, occasionally held as a charity event.

name: Compound Archery
description: Archery with a compound bow using cams, sights and release aids; the Olympic discipline at 70 m.

name: Contract Bridge
description: Trick-taking card game for four players in partnerships, played at clubs and world championships.

name: Coreeda
description: Australian Aboriginal team wrestling sport combining dance with combat in a 4.5 m circle, revived by the Coreeda Association of Australia.

name: Cornhole
description: American lawn game throwing beanbags at a hole in a raised board; standardized by the ACL with championship tournaments.

name: Cornish Hurling
description: Traditional Cornish game similar to rugby and Irish hurling, played with a small hard ball.

name: Counter-Strike
description: Tactical team first-person shooter (CS2) with million-dollar major tournaments in esports.

name: Cow Chip Throwing
description: Distance-throwing of dried cow dung pats; an old US fair event with official championships in Nebraska.

name: Cricket
description: Bat-and-ball game for two teams of eleven on an oval field, played from five-day Tests to 3-hour T20s; governed worldwide by the ICC.

name: Cricket ODI
description: One Day International cricket: each team bats one innings of 50 overs; World Cup every four years.

name: Cricket T20
description: Twenty20 cricket: fast three-hour matches with 20 overs per side and big franchise leagues like the IPL.

name: Croquet
description: Lawn game striking balls through hoops with a mallet; world championships governed by the World Croquet Federation.

name: Cross Triathlon
description: Off-road triathlon with mountain biking and trail running instead of road cycling and track running.

name: Cross-Country Equestrian
description: The cross-country phase of eventing: horse and rider gallop over solid fixed obstacles.

name: Cross-Country Mountain Biking
description: Mountain bike racing on a mass-start circuit with climbs, descents and technical sections.

name: Cross-Country Skiing
description: Endurance skiing on groomed tracks in classic or skating technique; Olympic since 1924.

name: Cross-Country Skiing Skiathlon
description: Cross-country ski race where athletes ski half the distance in classic and half in skating style.

name: Cross-Country Skiing Sprint
description: Cross-country ski sprint: short qualification heats and knockout finals on a 1 to 1.8 km course.

name: CrossFit
description: High-intensity fitness sport combining weightlifting, gymnastics and cardio; the CrossFit Games crown the fittest.

name: Crossminton
description: Racket sport formerly speed badminton, played with a heavy shuttle and no net on a 16 m court; Speedminton world rankings.

name: Crossnet
description: Four-player net game combining volleyball and four square; the ball is bounced off a tensioned net.

name: Crown Green Bowls
description: Lawn bowls played on a perfectly level 'crown green', the traditional British form of the game.

name: Crying Baby Festival
description: Japanese festival competition where babies are held up and the loudest cry wins.

name: Cuju
description: Ancient Chinese ball game with a leather ball and a small goal opening, considered an ancestor of football.

name: Curling
description: Ice sport where teams slide granite stones toward a target area (the house); nicknamed 'chess on ice'.

name: Cutting
description: Rodeo event where a horse and rider separate a single cow from the herd and hold it in a pen.

name: Cycle Speedway
description: Motorcycle speedway ridden on bicycles: races on a short oval cinder track without brakes.

name: Cycleball
description: Bicycle polo: two teams of two cyclists try to score goals with a ball using only their bikes.

name: Cycling
description: Bicycle racing on road, track, mountains or cyclo-cross courses; the Tour de France is the biggest race.

name: Cyclo-cross
description: Off-road cycling race on a short circuit of pavement, grass and mud, often carrying the bike over barriers.

name: Cyr Wheel
description: Gymnastics apparatus: a large metal hoop (Cyr wheel or German wheel) that the athlete rolls, balances and spins in.

name: Czech Handball
description: Handball variant from Czechia played 7v7 on a full-size court, historically popular in Central Europe.

name: DTM
description: Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters, Germany's top touring-car racing series with manufacturer teams.

name: Dahi Handi
description: Mumbai human pyramid competition of the Krishna festival, where young Govinda teams form tiers to break a hung pot of curd.

name: Dakar Rally
description: Legendary cross-country rally raid, originally Paris to Dakar and now in Saudi Arabia, for cars, bikes, quads and trucks.

name: Darts
description: Pub game and professional sport where players throw darts at a numbered board to reach exactly zero; PDC and BDO run majors.

name: Debate
description: Structured competitive argumentation where teams defend or oppose a motion, judged on logic, evidence and rhetoric.

name: Decathlon
description: Men's combined athletics event of ten disciplines over two days; the women's indoor equivalent is the heptathlon.

name: Dene Games
description: Traditional Dene events of the Arctic Winter Games: finger pull, snow snake, stick pull, hand games and pole push.

name: Disc Dog
description: Dog sport where handlers throw flying discs and dogs catch them, judged on distance, acrobatics and freestyle routines.

name: Disc Golf
description: Disc sport: golf played with flying discs on 9 or 18 hole courses; complete the course in the fewest throws governed by the PDGA

name: Diving
description: Aquatic sport of acrobatic dives from springboards and platforms, judged on difficulty, execution and entry.

name: Do-nothing Contest
description: Satirical competition where the winner is who can do nothing the longest; held annually in South Korea.

name: Dock Diving
description: Acrobatic diving from a dock or high platform into water, judged on difficulty, height and splash.

name: Dodge Juggle
description: Team dodgeball variant where players may also catch and throw multiple balls to eliminate opponents.

name: Dodgeball
description: Team sport in which players throw balls to eliminate opponents while dodging; world championships held since 2012 (WDBF).

name: Dog Sledding
description: Racing sled dogs pulling a sled over snow; famous races include the Iditarod and the Yukon Quest.

name: Dog Surfing
description: Novelty sport of dogs riding surfboards to shore; competitions such as the Surf Dog Surf-A-Thon in California.

name: Dota 2
description: Multiplayer online battle arena esport; The International is one of esports highest-prize tournaments.

name: Double Mini-Trampoline
description: Gymnastics discipline where athletes perform acrobatic bounces on a small double mini-trampoline.

name: Downhill Mountain Biking
description: Mountain biking down steep timed courses with jumps, rock gardens and banked turns.

name: Downhill Skateboarding
description: Longboarding or skateboarding down paved mountain roads at high speed with slides and tuck positions.

name: Drag Racing
description: Straight-line acceleration race over a quarter mile from a standing start; the NHRA is the top US series.

name: Dragon Boat Racing
description: Chinese-origin paddle sport of 10-20 paddlers in a decorated boat with a drummer; world championships (IDBF).

name: Draughts
description: Two-player board game (checkers in the US) where pieces move diagonally and capture by jumping; world championships exist.

name: Dressage
description: Equestrian 'horse ballet': horse and rider perform precise movements and figures, judged by points.

name: Drifting
description: Motorsport where drivers intentionally oversteer through corners in controlled slides, judged on angle, style and speed.

name: Drone Racing
description: FPV drone racing through obstacle courses at high speed, with world championships and big prize money.

name: Duathlon
description: Run-bike-run without swimming, raced from sprint to long distance world championships (World Triathlon).

name: Duck Herding
description: Competition where participants in small boats herd ducks through a water course.

name: Duplicate Bridge
description: Competitive contract bridge where the same hands are played at many tables and the scores are compared.

name: Dwile Flonking
description: Traditional English pub game where a beer-soaked cloth (dwile) is twirled overhead and thrown between teams.

name: E-Sports
description: Competitive video gaming as a sport, with world championships in games like League of Legends, Dota 2 and CS2.

name: Egg Tapping
description: Easter game and competition where two players tap hard-boiled eggs against each other; the uncracked egg wins.

name: Electrician Games
description: Trade competitions for electricians combining practical installation tasks and theory tests.

name: Endurance Riding
description: Equestrian long-distance horse racing over 80 to 160 km in one day, with veterinary checks for horse welfare.

name: Enduro
description: Motorcycle off-road endurance racing over long courses with timed special stages.

name: Enduro Mountain Biking
description: Mountain bike racing of timed downhill special stages linked by untimed transfer stages over one or more days (EMB/Enduro World Series).

name: English Billiards
description: Cue sport on a large snooker-sized table with three balls (white, spotted white, red), scored by cannons and pots.

name: Equestrian Vaulting
description: Gymnastics on a moving horse guided by a lunger; an FEI discipline with world championships.

name: Eton Wall Game
description: Traditional Eton College football played against a wall with a scrummage for the ball; contested since the 18th century.

name: Eventing
description: Equestrian triathlon of dressage, cross-country and show jumping on the same horse.

name: Excel World Championship
description: Esports competition for Microsoft Excel: solving complex spreadsheet problems against the clock.

name: Extreme Ironing
description: Novelty activity of ironing in extreme locations such as cliffs and underwater; world championship first held in 2002.

name: Extreme Mountain Unicycling
description: Unicycling off-road in the mountains with big drops, rock gardens and trials obstacles.

name: Extreme Speed Yodeling
description: Novelty competition combining fast running with yodeling, held at Swiss alpine events.

name: Face Slapping
description: Combat sport where two competitors slap each other with an open hand; the first to fall or look away loses.

name: Fastpitch Softball
description: Softball discipline with fast windmill pitching; the women's form was Olympic 1996-2008 and 2020 with its own WBSC rulebook.

name: Fencing

name: Pelota Purépecha

name: Pickleball

name: Pigeon Racing

name: Pillow Fighting

name: Pinball

name: Platform Tennis

name: Pop Tennis

name: Popdarts

name: Pétanque

name: Quadrathlon
description: Combined event of four disciplines, for example canoeing, running, shooting and riding.

name: Rabbit Show Jumping
description: Pet sport of rabbits jumping over miniature hurdles on a course; Scandinavian-led competitions.

name: Racquetball

name: Rafting
description: Navigating whitewater rapids on an inflatable raft, as recreation and competition.

description: Tactical esports shooter built on destructible environments; annual world invitationals.

name: Recurve Archery

name: Reining

name: River Surfing

name: Road Cycling

name: Rugby Tens

name: Schlagball

name: Schutzhund
description: Dog protection sport (also IPO/Mondioring) testing tracking, obedience and protection with a decoy.

name: Schwingen

name: Scrabble

name: Sepak Takraw

name: Sipa

name: Sitting Volleyball

description: Pool discipline where the rack must be cleared as fast as possible against the clock.

description: Competitive climbing disciplines lead, boulder and speed; combined Olympic event since Tokyo 2020.

name: Ssireum

description: Esports real-time strategy standard of Korean pro leagues and world championship system.

name: Steeplechase
description: Olympic athletics event over 3000 m of barriers and a water jump on the track.

description: Bavarian strength sport: holding a heavy stone mug with a fully straight arm for as long as possible.

description: Pool game (14.1 continuous) where each pocketed ball scores a point and a set total must be reached.

description: Ball hockey played on pavement without skates; international federations run world championships.

description: Gravity racing lying feet first on an extended board down closed mountain roads.

description: Calisthenics in public parks on bars and rings, with strength and freestyle competitions.

description: Women's strongman contests with yoke, log press, deadlift and atlas stone events.

name: Supermoto
description: Motorcycle racing combining motocross and road racing on tracks with dirt and asphalt sections.

name: Surf Lifesaving
description: Competitive surf lifesaving with swimming, board and tube rescue races on the beach.

name: Surfing
description: Water sport of riding breaking waves on a board while standing; Olympic since Tokyo 2020.

description: Football played in bogs and mud pits; format born in Finnish swamps with world championships.

name: Systema
description: Russian martial art and movement system focused on breathing, relaxation and natural movement.

name: Table Football

name: Table Shuffleboard
description: Sliding pucks down a waxed table into scoring zones, played in bars and leagues (deck and table).

name: Table Tennis
description: Racket sport with a small ball over a net on a table; Olympic since 1988 and one of the fastest ball sports.

name: Taekkyeon
description: Traditional Korean martial art with flowing kicks, trips and acrobatic movements, often performed to music.

name: Taekwondo

name: Taekwondo WT

name: Tai Chi Chuan
description: Chinese internal martial art with slow, flowing movements, practiced for health and self-defense.

name: Tamburello
description: Italian field racquet sport striking a small ball with a round tambourine-shaped paddle.

name: Tang Soo Do
description: Korean martial art influenced by karate and Chinese arts, with forms (hyung) and sparring.

name: Target Archery

name: Tchoukball

name: Teddy Bear Toss

name: Tejo

name: Ten-Pin Bowling

name: Tennis

name: Tent Pegging
description: Equestrian sport where riders at full gallop pick up a small ground target (peg) with a sword or lance.

name: Teqvoly
description: Teqball variant played like volleyball over a curved table using feet, head and chest.

name: Texas Hold'em Poker

name: Thang-Ta
description: Martial art of the Manipur region in India with sword, spear and dagger techniques.

name: Three-Cushion Billiards

name: Throwball

name: Toe Wrestling
description: British novelty wrestling of locked big toes in a ring; world championships held at Fenny Bentley.

name: Tomahawk Throwing

name: Top Fuel Drag Racing

name: Touch Rugby

name: Touchtennis

name: Track Cycling

name: Track Cycling Elimination Race

name: Tractor Pulling

name: Trail Orienteering
description: Orienteering with precise map reading in complex terrain, often with a time limit per control.

name: Trampoline

name: Trampoline Dodgeball
description: Dodgeball on trampoline courts, played in parks and leagues as a fitness format.

name: Trap Shooting
description: Shotgun discipline where clay pigeons are launched away from the shooter at random angles.

name: Trial Motorcycling
description: Motorcycle trials: riding over rocky, steep sections without touching the ground; each foot-down is a penalty.

name: Triathle
description: Three-discipline competition of shooting, swimming and running, derived from military training.

name: Triathlon
description: Swim-bike-run endurance race from sprint to Ironman distance; Olympic since Sydney 2000.

name: Tricking
description: Acrobatic sport combining martial arts kicks, gymnastics flips and trampoline skills, often outdoors.

name: Tricklining
description: Slacklining with acrobatic tricks: flips, bounces and poses on a tensioned webbing.

name: Tug of War
description: Team rope-pull strength contest of eight per side; TWIF world championships and former Olympic sport.

name: Tumbling
description: Acrobatic gymnastics along a sprung track; world championship and World Games discipline.

name: Tuna Throwing
description: Australian festival event where teams throw a frozen tuna over a bar at the Tunarama in Port Lincoln.

name: Turkey Bowling
description: Bowling variant using a frozen turkey as the ball, popular at US charity events.

name: Ulama
description: Prehispanic Mesoamerican hip-ball game descended from the Aztec ullamaliztli, still played in Mexican communities.

name: Ultimate
description: Non-contact team sport played with a flying disc; players may not run with the disc and the game is self-refereed (Spirit of the Game, WFDF).

name: Ultimate Tazer Ball
description: Team ball game with an electrified ball that players must carry, pass and score with.

name: Underwater Cycling
description: Novelty sport of riding a bicycle at the bottom of a swimming pool in diving gear.

name: Underwater Hockey
description: Breath-hold team sport pushing a puck along the pool bottom with short sticks; CMAS world championships.

name: Underwater Ice Hockey
description: Ice hockey played under the ice of a frozen lake, with divers and upside-down goals.

name: Underwater Orienteering
description: CMAS sport of navigating underwater courses by compass and depth with monofin swims.

name: Underwater Rugby
description: Three-dimensional underwater team ball sport of getting the saltwater-filled ball into the basket.

name: Underwater Target Shooting
description: Spearfishing at stationary targets underwater, scored by accuracy and target zones.

name: Unicycle Hockey
description: Team hockey played mounted on unicycles, five per side without body checking; IUF world championships.

name: Unicycle Polo
description: Polo played on unicycles with mallets on a smaller pitch, requiring balance and stick skill.

name: Valorant
description: Tactical esports shooter from Riot Games with character abilities; world championship circuit.

name: Varpa
description: Gotland (Sweden) throwing game where players throw stones to knock over or hit a wooden peg (varpa) at distance.

name: Varzesh-e Bastani
description: Iranian ritual athletics of the zurkhaneh with meels, sang and kabadeh, fused with Persian heroic poetry; UNESCO intangible heritage.

name: Vinkensport
description: Belgian bird sport (vinkenzetting): male chaffinches compete to make the most calls in one hour.

name: Volata
description: Traditional game of the Aosta Valley in Italy, similar to calcio storico, played with an oval ball.

name: Volleyball
description: Team sport over a net where players hit the ball into the opponent's court; Olympic since 1964, 6v6 indoors.

name: Vovinam
description: Vietnamese martial art combining hard and soft techniques with forms, sparring and weapon training.

name: Wado-Ryu Karate
description: Japanese karate style founded by Hironori Otsuka, combining jujutsu with karate and emphasizing evasion.

name: Wakeboarding
description: Water board sport riding the boat wake with airs and flips; world wake championships.

name: Wakeskating
description: Water sport like wakeboarding but on a wakeskate without bindings, towed by a boat.

name: Wakesurfing
description: Surfing on the wake of a boat with a small surf-style board, without a tow rope after the start.

name: Walking Football
description: Football for older players: walking only, no running, no contact; growing rapidly worldwide.

name: Walking Rugby
description: Non-contact rugby where players walk and are tagged instead of tackled, for older or less mobile players.

name: Wallyball
description: Volleyball variant played in a racquetball or squash court using all four walls; very fast rallies.

name: Washer Toss
description: Lawn game of tossing washers at a cup, can or stake to score points within sets to 11 or 21.

name: Water Polo
description: Team sport in a pool where players swim and throw a ball into the opponent's goal; Olympic since 1900.

name: Water Volleyball
description: Volleyball played in shallow water on a reduced net, popular as aqua fitness and recreational club play.

name: Watermelon Seed Spitting
description: Competition to spit watermelon seeds the farthest; a world championship is held in Texas.

name: Weight Over Bar
description: Highland Games heavy event throwing a 56 lb weight over a rising bar; tallest clearance wins.

name: Weight Pulling Dog Sport
description: Dog sport in which harnessed dogs pull a weighted cart or sled over a short course for percentage records.

name: Weight for Height
description: Strength contest where a weight is lifted relative to the athlete's height, a pound-for-height style event.

name: Weightlifting
description: Olympic strength sport with two lifts, snatch and clean and jerk, across weight classes.

name: Welsh Handball
description: Traditional Welsh handball (pela Gymreig) played against a wall in one-wall and four-wall formats.

name: Wheel Gymnastics
description: Gymnastics on the German wheel (rhönrad): rolling, vaulting and balancing inside a large hoop.

name: Wheelbarrow Olympics
description: Festival team races pushing wheelbarrows through obstacle and cargo challenges, for charity events.

name: Wheelchair Basketball
description: Paralympic basketball played in sports wheelchairs by teams of five with a points classification system.

name: Wheelchair Curling
description: Curling adapted for wheelchair athletes, delivering stones from a fixed position without a push.

name: Wheelchair Fencing
description: Fencing for wheelchair athletes on a fixed frame; épée and foil are Paralympic events.

name: Wheelchair Handball
description: Handball adapted for wheelchair athletes, played on a smaller court with four players per side.

name: Wheelchair Rugby
description: Paralympic coed contact sport for quadriplegic athletes mixing rugby, basketball and handball elements.

name: Wheelchair Tennis
description: Paralympic tennis in which the ball may bounce twice before being hit; ITF majors include Wimbledon.

name: Wife Carrying
description: Obstacle race carrying a partner, world championships against the clock at Sonkajarvi, Finland since 1992.

name: Wildwater Canoeing
description: Canoeing or kayaking down fast-flowing whitewater rivers, racing through rapids.

name: Windsurfing
description: Sailing sport combining a board and a sail; windsurfers ride waves and race; Olympic since 1984.

name: Wine Slinging
description: Competition to sling or spit wine the farthest, held at wine festivals in Spain and elsewhere.

name: Wing Chun
description: Chinese martial art famous for close-range strikes, 'sticky hands' training and the wooden dummy form.

name: Wing Foiling
description: Foil board sport where the rider holds a handheld wing that propels the hydrofoil board over the water.

name: Wingsuit Flying
description: Skydiving in a fabric wingsuit that greatly increases glide; includes proximity flying and acrobatics.

name: Winter Triathlon
description: Winter triathlon variant: running, mountain biking and cross-country skiing on snow.

name: Women's Australian Rules Football
description: Australian rules football played by women; the AFLW is the top professional league since 2017.

name: Woodball
description: Sport from Taiwan played with a wooden ball through gates on fairways, between golf and croquet.

name: Working Cow Horse
description: Rodeo event testing a horse's 'cow sense': separating, turning and holding a single cow.

name: World Black Pudding Throwing Championships
description: Annual competition in Ramsbottom, England: throwing black puddings to knock over stacks of Yorkshire puddings.

name: World Chase Tag
description: Competitive tag league with one-on-one chases on a parkour quadrangle; WCT championships.

name: World Endurance Championship
description: FIA endurance racing series for prototypes and GT cars, including the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

name: World Gurning Championships
description: Face-pulling world championship held at the Egremont Crab Fair in Cumbria since the fair began in 1267.

name: World Porridge Eating Championship
description: Annual porridge-eating speed contest held in Dorking, England.

name: World Rally Championship
description: FIA rally series with events on gravel, snow and asphalt worldwide; WRC since 1973.

name: World Stone Skimming Championships
description: Annual competition on the Isle of Easdale, Scotland: skipping stones across water for the most skips.

name: Worm Charming
description: Vibrating worms from a marked plot of earth in the shortest time; world championships in Nantwich, UK.

name: Wrestling
description: Olympic combat sport of grappling, throws and pins in weight classes; freestyle and Greco-Roman styles.

name: Wushu Sanda
description: Full-contact Chinese wushu sparring with punches, kicks and throws; world championships exist.

name: Wushu Taolu
description: Choreographed wushu forms with acrobatic jumps and weapon routines, judged like gymnastics.

name: Xare
description: Basque pelota variant (joko garbi) played with a basket (xare) on the hand; extremely fast.

name: Xiangqi
description: Chinese chess on a 9x10 board with cannons and a river; one of the most played board games in the world.

name: Yak Racing
description: Traditional races with decorated yaks at festivals in Mongolia, Kyrgyzstan and China.

name: Yukigassen
description: Japanese competitive snowball fight of seven-a-side teams played on a snow court with helmets.

name: Zorbing
description: Rolling downhill inside a giant transparent plastic sphere for fun at commercial adventure sites.
